title: Deployment rhythm optimizer and space reservation protocol for runtime/console/api
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Create an opinionated playbook (Deployment Rhythm Optimizer) that standardizes how we reserve launch slots across Runtime, Console, and API teams and a lightweight Space Reservation Protocol to reduce cross-team contention. Scope includes a calendar-as-code convention, slot-tenancy rules, capacity hedging heuristics, an ownership matrix for cutover windows, and automation templates for calendar booking and alerting. Deliverables: playbook doc, calendar-as-code templates, a small service to manage reservations (MVP), onboarding checklist, stakeholder runbook, and a rollout plan. Success metrics: reduce calendar collisions by 80% within first quarter, decrease last-minute capacity escalations by 60%, and hit >=90% successful canaries in reserved slots. Risks: institutional resistance to new cadence, edge cases around burst capacity for Dedicated customers, and region-specific blackout windows. Key stakeholders: Runtime PM/ENG, Console PM/ENG, API platform lead, SRE, ReleaseOps, Solutions Engineering.

comments: 2026-03-09 Ava Martinez: Created ticket. Rationale: recurring friction when multiple teams request overlapping launch windows (observed incidents in Feb and Mar). Linked to runtime-incident-2026-02 on PagerDuty and the postmortem (https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RT-2026-02-postmortem).

Github proto branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/launch-reservoir/pull/12

2026-03-15 Product review: Agreed to pilot two launches in dedicated slots: runtime-model-swap (canary) and console-feature-flags. Assigning owners and acceptance champions. Next: schedule cross-team alignment workshop 2026-03-24.
